method: Fast read only (read.mjs, 22-46 s a site), one juror in the main session (Fable 5.2): read.md and read-sheet.png of each. No inspector run, so craft is judged by eye and contrast, layout shift and tap targets are not measured. ref-0026 and ref-0028 open only after a consent panel and an entrance button; the reader pressed them. Only the first 6,000-11,000px of ref-0026 (20,000px) and ref-0028 (43,000px) were seen. Phones: ref-0026 and ref-0028 showed only their loader in the phone frame.

ref-0025.business: OUTFIT by hellohello: a design studio's own apparel and accessories shop. Action: add to bag.

reasons.business: Shop and Bag stay in the corner, every product carries its name and price in small red type. The product page is plain (owner's note); no sizes, materials or delivery on the listing.
reasons.customer: A shopper sees the whole range with prices at once. What the brand is, who makes it and why it costs this is one line at the very bottom.
reasons.story: Range, then one statement ('Made to be worn. Or judged. Or both.'), then the maker. Short, in one voice.
reasons.clarity: Black loader with a counter for about 4 seconds before anything shows. After that: paper ground, products, prices.
reasons.distinctiveness: Products are laid out at three scales with empty cells between them: a row of four, then a thumbnail pair beside one bag half the screen wide. One red for every word, tight grotesk, a statement as wide as the column, '©26' as a mark. It does not look like a shop template.
reasons.craft: By eye: one grid broken on purpose, captions aligned to pictures, one red, one typeface. Not measured.

claims.claim: very un-template; typography play makes it different
claims.evidence: one tight grotesk in one red at two extremes (12px captions, a statement about 100px tall), the loader's OUTFIT lettering with photographs stacked in its gap

claims.claim: product arrangement differs from the usual
claims.evidence: floor.mjs: 4 of 5 sections composed (scale contrast, staggered, overlap, leaving the frame); 19 pictures
the product page was not read

ref-0025.motion: lenis smooth scroll; a 4 s counter loader with stacked photographs in the wordmark; hover on a product changes transform and opacity; no scroll choreography.
problems: Almost nothing about the brand or the product beyond name and price
keep: scale-scatter: one range at three sizes on the grid with empty cells and small captions
One colour for all type, captions included
statement-band: one sentence as large as the column, a rule above, a mark at the right
A wordmark with photographs stacked in its gap

ref-0026.business: Capitolium: a jersey made together by Toulouse FC and Stade Toulousain (with Nike), named after the city's Capitole. Action: buy the jersey (the club shops).

reasons.business: 'Plus qu'un maillot, le symbole de notre cité' and both jerseys on pedestals arrive within three screens. Where to buy was not seen in the part read.
reasons.customer: A supporter gets the meaning of the shirt: the building, the arcades, the story behind each detail. Price, sizes and availability were not seen.
reasons.story: An entrance, the Capitole from the air, the square, the claim, the jerseys, then numbered chapters ('Les arcades') that walk through the building. The visitor is led, one thing at a time.
reasons.clarity: A grey loader, a cookie panel and an 'Entrer' button stand before the content. Inside, each screen says one thing.
reasons.distinctiveness: Marble, slate and gold; engraved capitals with a script word that slides across the picture; arched windows cut from the building's own arcades that open into the scene. The place is the design system.
reasons.craft: By eye: pinned chapters that hand over cleanly, type and pictures on one axis. 12 sticky panels, 8 videos, 3 WebGL canvases: heavy; not measured.

claims.claim: scrolling experience very good and comfortable; it carries you into each story of the brand and product
claims.evidence: read.mjs: 12 sticky panels of 900px; the hero text at ×0.12-0.65 of scroll speed; chapter title letters at ×0.09-0.25; one chapter moves sideways (track ←513px per step)

ref-0026.motion: Pinned full-screen chapters; text and title letters moving slower than the page (×0.1-0.65); arched windows where the middle one widens to full screen; a chapter that travels sideways; transitions 0.3-0.6 s, cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1).
problems: Three gates before content: loader, cookie panel, 'Entrer'
Where to buy and the price were not found in the part read
Heavy: 8 videos and 3 WebGL canvases; the phone frame showed only the loader
keep: window-open: arched windows onto one scene, one widening to fill the screen
horizontal-track: a pinned chapter that moves sideways
type-over-picture: a script word sliding across the picture
pedestal: the product on a plinth with the title behind it
An identity taken from one place (its arches, marble and inscription)

ref-0027.business: L'Oiseau Dé: a Framer template for a beauty and cosmetics shop (the page offers the template, 'Get for free'). As a shop: browse categories, buy products.

reasons.business: Categories, featured products with prices and a brand list are all there. It is a template: the business is placeholder content, and the fixed button sells the template.
reasons.customer: A shopper sees what is sold (skincare, cosmetics, face health) and three products with prices; nothing on ingredients, skin types or delivery.
reasons.story: Hero, a line on what the shop is, categories, two brand values, products, brands, footer: orderly, without a turn.
reasons.clarity: One name, one picture, plain labels. Easy at every step.
reasons.distinctiveness: Carried by the photographs (owner's note). The layout adds to it: picture tiles alternate with colour tiles holding a small label; small pictures step down across a green field; the name runs across the bottom of the hero. Greens, lime and cream. Recognisable, though the parts are familiar.
reasons.craft: By eye: even cells, one type family, consistent crops. Not measured.

claims.claim: aesthetic and minimalist, but it wins through good pictures
claims.evidence: every screen is led by a portrait or product photograph; without them the page is colour tiles and labels

claims.claim: the layout feels different because it is not monotonous
claims.evidence: hero with type over the picture, a marquee, a checkerboard of picture and colour tiles, stepped pictures on a field, a product row, a list in large type: six arrangements

ref-0027.motion: Framer Motion; 5 sticky elements (sections pinned at 830px); a marquee band; one CSS scroll-driven rule; transitions 0.4 s.
problems: A template: the business content is placeholder
Depends wholly on photographs of this quality
A fixed 'Get for free' button over every screen
keep: checker-fields: picture tiles alternating with colour tiles that hold a small label
stepped-drift: small pictures stepping down across a field beside a short statement
type-over-picture: the name on the lower edge of the hero
index-in-type: the brand list set as large type

ref-0028.business: Indigo: a contemporary jewellery house; '5 tales of being', five collections told as chapters. Action: request info on a piece.

reasons.business: Each tale ends in a product (Selene ring) with 'Request info'. No price, no shop; 43,000px of page.
reasons.customer: A buyer learns the idea of each collection and sees the piece worn and alone. Material, size, price and how to buy are behind a request.
reasons.story: An invitation ('Before the gesture, there is a sound'), then five tales, each with a cover, a title in cut letters, a text, pictures, the piece. The same order every time, so the visitor learns it.
reasons.clarity: A violet splash and a choice about sound before the content; a cookie panel stayed over the lower right of every frame in this read.
reasons.distinctiveness: Lettering cut like paper for INDIGO and each tale's title; black, white and one violet; photographs at very different sizes with a ring floating across them. You know whose it is while scrolling (owner's note).
reasons.craft: By eye: photographs of one shoot, generous white, clean hand-overs between chapters. One WebGL canvas, smooth scrolling; not measured.

claims.claim: after entering, a scrolling experience per category with smooth transitions and good photographs; you feel the brand while scrolling
claims.evidence: read.mjs: 10 sticky elements, covers pinned at 900px, pictures moving sideways (←496 to ←728px a step), a progress bar per chapter; lenis

ref-0028.motion: lenis; chapter covers pinned while content scrolls over; pictures entering sideways; text slightly faster than the page (×1.16-1.34); a chapter progress bar; an endless ring spinner and scroll indicator.
problems: A sound gate and a splash before content
No price or way to buy, only 'Request info'
Very long (43,000px); the phone frame showed only the splash
keep: chapter-cover: every chapter opens on a full-screen cover with a title in the brand's lettering
offset-pair: two pictures of different sizes, staggered, text in the gap
object-thread: the jewel floating across the chapter
Lettering as the brand: cut-paper letters for the name and every title
The same order in every chapter, so the visitor learns the page
